Core_Approach: Meta-theory integrating multiple perspectives with non-reductionist epistemology

Core_Approach: All Quadrants, All Levels framework with spiritual development focus
Strengths: Comprehensive framework; spiritual integration; developmental perspective
Key_Limitations: Eastern mysticism bias; overly complex; limited cultural validity

Strengths: Addresses postmodern limitations; practical reconstruction orientation
Key_Limitations: Lacks clear methodology; may fall into relativism; still developing
Relationship_to_NRP: Parallel attempt to move beyond postmodernism with reconstruction

Key_Limitations: Western-centric despite claims; simplifies complex cultural factors
Relationship_to_NRP: Incorporated as levels/stages component within NRP framework

Core_Approach: Emergence and self-organization in complex adaptive systems
Strengths: Strong scientific foundation; explains emergence and adaptation
Key_Limitations: Mathematical complexity; may not address meaning and values adequately
Relationship_to_NRP: Supports emergentism claims; provides scientific grounding

Core_Approach: Holistic understanding of interconnected systems and feedback loops
Strengths: Well-established methodology; broad applicability across disciplines
Key_Limitations: Can be mechanistic; may not capture subjective experience fully
Relationship_to_NRP: Influences systemic thinking; incorporated in lower-right quadrant

Core_Approach: Multiple valid perspectives, deconstruction of grand narratives
Strengths: Challenges dominant paradigms; includes marginalized perspectives
Key_Limitations: Leads to paralysis and nihilism; difficulty making truth claims
Relationship_to_NRP: Critiqued by NRP as incomplete; used as developmental stage example

Core_Approach: Reality reducible to fundamental physical processes and laws
Strengths: Empirical rigor; technological applications; predictive power
Key_Limitations: Reductionist; eliminates meaning, consciousness, and subjective experience
Relationship_to_NRP: Explicitly rejected as reductionist; contrasted with NRP approach

Core_Approach: Reality as process and becoming rather than static being
Strengths: Avoids static categories; emphasizes change and development
Key_Limitations: Difficult to operationalize; may lack clear practical applications
Relationship_to_NRP: Philosophical alignment with emergentism and dynamic development

Core_Approach: Cognition as embodied action rather than internal representation
Strengths: Embodied cognition research; challenges representationalist assumptions
Key_Limitations: Limited scope; may not address higher-order cognitive processes
Relationship_to_NRP: Supportive of embodied cognition aspects; challenges pure rationalism
